description: Next.js app router + Supabase + Stripe + LLM chat starter with 16 planted vulnerabilities and 11 decoys. `anchor` is a substring that must appear inside `lines` (checked by bench/test); `locations` lists extra places that also count for the same item.

items.title: support_tickets table created without row level security
profiles select policy is using (true): every visitor reads every email and Stripe customer id
Service-role Supabase client built in a client component; key inlined into the bundle via next.config env
Unauthenticated route (outside the middleware matcher) returns every customer's email and Stripe id via the service-role client
Order lookup by id with the service-role client and no owner filter (IDOR)
Checkout unit_amount and product name taken from the request body
Stripe webhook parses the body without verifying the signature; anyone can mark orders paid
LLM chat endpoint with no authentication, no rate limit and no token cap (unbounded spend)
SQL built by interpolating q and sort across a multi-line template literal
SSRF: unauthenticated route fetches a caller-supplied URL and returns the body
Mail provider API key hardcoded in source
Admin API token lives in a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable, so it ships to every browser
Open redirect after login: next query parameter used unvalidated
Mass assignment: whole request body written to profiles, caller can set role to admin
pull_request_target workflow checks out PR head and runs its code with repository secrets
Store admin credentials committed in an e2e setup file that targets the production URL
Invoices route has no auth call and no owner filter
items.why_safe: middleware.ts matcher covers /api/invoices/:path* and rejects anonymous callers; the query uses the user-session client, and the invoices table has an owner-only RLS select policy.

items.title: new Function built from RULE_BODY
items.why_safe: RULE_BODY is a module-level string literal, not attacker-influenced.

items.title: Multi-line SQL template with interpolated values
items.why_safe: It is a tagged template for the postgres library, which turns each ${} into a bound parameter.

items.title: Webhook route with no visible signature check in the handler
items.why_safe: verifyWebhook in lib/webhooks/verify.ts checks HMAC-SHA256 with timingSafeEqual and a timestamp tolerance before the body is parsed.

items.title: Supabase key in a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable used from the browser
items.why_safe: It is the anon key, which is designed to be public; access is limited by RLS.

items.title: Redirect target comes from a query parameter
items.why_safe: safeRedirect only returns paths from a fixed allowlist, otherwise '/'.

items.title: Service-role client created at module scope
items.why_safe: The module imports server-only, so a client component importing it fails the build; the key is never inlined (but see vs-03 for the separate leak).

items.title: NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable with ADMIN in its name
items.why_safe: It holds a public support mailbox address, not a credential.

items.title: Service-role route with no user session
items.why_safe: It requires a CRON_SECRET bearer token compared in constant time; it is not user-reachable.

items.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML
items.why_safe: The HTML is a constant string with no interpolated or user-controlled data.

items.title: Database URL with a password in an env file
items.why_safe: Placeholder credentials for the local Supabase dev stack on 127.0.0.1 in an example file that is meant to be copied, not a real secret.
